title: Boston Baked Beans
subtitle: slow-cooked beans in a sweet and smoky sauce
excerpt: White beans slowly baked with bacon, treacle, and mustard in a sweet, smoky sauce. This is a deeply satisfying side dish for BBQ or a simple meal with cornbread. It gets better the longer it cooks.
sourceNotes: Boston baked beans date to the colonial era, when Puritan settlers learned to bake beans with bear fat and maple syrup from Native Americans. Treacle and pork came later.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day. Reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: If using dried beans, soak them overnight and parboil before baking. This dish rewards patience. The longer it bakes, the deeper the flavour and the more tender the beans.

items.prepNote: use navy beans (dried, soaked overnight) -- or 2 x 400g tins of cannellini beans, drained

content.text: Preheat the oven to 150C (fan 130C / gas 2). Cook the bacon in a large oven-safe pot until the fat renders.
Add the onion. Cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the brown sugar, treacle, mustard, vinegar, and tomato puree.
Add the beans and pour in enough stock to just cover them. Stir well.
Cover with a lid or foil and bake for 2 hours. Check every 45 minutes and add a splash of water if they look dry.
Remove the lid for the last 30 minutes to thicken the sauce. Season and serve.

items.symptom: Beans are still firm after 2 hours
items.cause: Old dried beans or insufficient liquid
items.fix: Old dried beans can take much longer to soften. If using tinned beans, they will be tender in 1 to 1.5 hours. Add more stock and keep cooking.

items.cause: Too much liquid or lid on throughout
items.fix: Remove lid and bake uncovered for another 20 to 30 minutes until thickened.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick and catching
items.cause: Too little liquid or oven too hot
items.fix: Add a splash of stock or water and reduce the oven temperature slightly. Stir gently.

content.text: Boston baked beans trace back to colonial New England, where Puritan settlers adopted a Native American method of slow-cooking beans in clay pots. The Puritans added pork and sweeteners. Boston became so associated with the dish that the city earned the nickname Beantown. It has been a staple of American home cooking ever since.
